title: Rationality: From AI to Zombies
pitch: The Sequences: 333 essays on thinking clearly, changing your mind and why building AI with the right values is so hard. The book that grew the rationalist and AI safety communities.
toc_note: Six books, 26 lettered sequences. The guide covers each sequence.

chapters.g: Cognitive biases: the systematic ways human thinking goes wrong, and why knowing about them is only the start.
Beliefs that do not pay rent in predictions, and beliefs people hold to signal, not to be true.
Treat confusion as a clue that your model is wrong. Strong evidence should surprise a wrong model.
Why 'magic' or 'emergence' are not explanations, and how to tell real answers from curiosity stoppers.
How we avoid uncomfortable conclusions by finding reasons that happen to suit us.
chapters.part: Book II: How to Actually Change Your Mind

chapters.g: Why political arguments make smart people worse at reasoning.
chapters.part: Book II: How to Actually Change Your Mind

chapters.g: The difference between reasoning to a conclusion and finding arguments for one you already chose.
chapters.part: Book II: How to Actually Change Your Mind

chapters.g: You cannot choose to believe something you know is false without damaging your thinking.
chapters.part: Book II: How to Actually Change Your Mind

chapters.g: Anchoring, cached thoughts and how to actually think about a problem instead of repeating answers.
chapters.part: Book II: How to Actually Change Your Mind

chapters.g: How groups and ideas can become cult like, and the warning signs.
chapters.part: Book II: How to Actually Change Your Mind

chapters.g: The hardest part: actually giving up a belief you were wrong about.
chapters.part: Book II: How to Actually Change Your Mind

chapters.t: L. The Simple Math of Evolution
chapters.g: Evolution as an optimisation process with no foresight, and what it teaches about optimisers in general.
chapters.part: Book III: The Machine in the Ghost

chapters.g: Why goals are fragile and how optimisers can satisfy a goal in ways nobody wanted. A foundation for alignment.
chapters.part: Book III: The Machine in the Ghost

chapters.t: N. A Human's Guide to Words
chapters.g: How words and categories can mislead, and how to use them well.
chapters.part: Book III: The Machine in the Ghost

chapters.g: The universe follows laws, and good reasoning respects that.
Explaining things in terms of their parts, without explaining them away.

chapters.t: Q. Joy in the Merely Real
chapters.g: Science does not drain the world of wonder. Real things can be awe inspiring.
Minds, consciousness and identity seen from a physical point of view (including the zombies of the title).

chapters.t: S. Quantum Physics and Many Worlds
chapters.g: An introduction to quantum mechanics and the many worlds interpretation, as a case study in reasoning.
Where the scientific method stops and good reasoning has to go further.
Why simple statements of what we want are not our real values.
Human values are complex and fragile, so a powerful AI with almost right values could be a disaster.
Taking numbers seriously in ethics, such as scope insensitivity and how to help the most people.
Yudkowsky's own story of how he was wrong about AI and changed his mind toward safety.
On trying things that seem impossible, and doing more than 'trying'.

chapters.t: Z. The Craft and the Community
chapters.g: How to build communities that practise and improve rationality together.

ideas: Beliefs should be about predicting the world, not about who we are.
Optimisation processes, like evolution, find solutions nobody intended.
Human values are complex and fragile.
Changing your mind is a skill you can practise.

args.a: Clear thinking is needed to see AI risk clearly.
args.c: Critics say the community this book grew can be insular and overconfident in its own models.

questions: What is a belief you hold that does not 'pay rent' in predictions?
How does the evolution sequence relate to AI training?
Have you ever let go of a belief you cared about? What made it possible?

quiz.q: How many books make up Rationality: From AI to Zombies?
Which sequence most directly supports alignment worries?
quiz.w: They argue goals are fragile and values are complex.

o: Treat it as a sign your model may be wrong
quiz.w: Confusion is evidence about your map, not the territory.
